purpose: Python language/stdlib feature inventory for AI coding agents; emphasizes underused high-leverage features.
authority_note: Official Python docs are authoritative for language semantics; underuse classifications here are heuristic, not GitHub-wide measured frequencies.

soft_keywords.context: match statement wildcard; otherwise normal identifier by convention

soft_keywords.use: PEP 695 type alias syntax; keep compatibility in mind

operators_and_delimiters.notes: Prefer clarity over clever arithmetic operator overloads.
Expression @ is matrix multiplication; leading @ line is decorator syntax.
Use rich comparison dunders carefully and return NotImplemented for unsupported types.
Use for None, sentinels, identity; not for value equality.
Short-circuiting; avoid abusing truthiness for ambiguous domain state.
Also used by sets; | is type union in annotations and dict merge on dicts.
Use sparingly for expensive predicate reuse; avoid dense one-liners.
Avoid in-place mutation at domain boundaries unless intentional.
Semicolon is legal but usually harms readability; colon defines suites/slices/dicts.
Use implicit line joining inside these instead of backslashes.
Useful for explicit adaptation layers; avoid hiding shape changes.
Useful as placeholder or multidimensional slicing; do not leave in real code silently.

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: Module public API with __all__ plus underscore helpers
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Makes the intended import surface obvious to humans and AI agents; prevents random code from reaching into internals.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.use_when: A module/package has public classes/functions and private helpers.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.avoid_when: Tiny throwaway scripts with no reuse.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Expose only intended API via __all__; prefix internal helpers with _; do not import _helpers from outside the module.

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True, kw_only=True)
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Gives AI a compact, typed, immutable value object; reduces accidental mutation and noisy boilerplate.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.use_when: Domain records, config objects, parsed packets, result objects.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.avoid_when: Objects require identity mutation, ORM models, or dynamic attributes.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Prefer frozen slots dataclasses for value objects and command/result packets.

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: NewType for domain IDs
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Prevents AI from mixing customer_id, matter_id, route_id, and file_id as generic strings.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.avoid_when: Trivial scripts or values genuinely interchangeable.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Use NewType or small dataclass wrappers for IDs crossing module boundaries.

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: Protocol for dependency boundaries
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Lets agents code against small behavior contracts instead of concrete infrastructure classes.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.use_when: Adapters for filesystem, API clients, repositories, clocks, random sources, model clients.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.avoid_when: One-off internal code with no test seam.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Define Protocols for side-effect dependencies and inject them into public workflow classes.

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: TypedDict at JSON/API boundaries
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Clarifies external dict shapes without pretending loose JSON is a domain object.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.use_when: Parsing JSON, CLI packets, API payloads, config files.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.avoid_when: Internal domain logic; convert to dataclass after validation.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Use TypedDict for raw dict boundary shapes; convert to dataclasses for internal domain logic.

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: StrEnum / Enum / Literal for explicit states
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Replaces magic strings with checked state vocabulary.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.use_when: Statuses, modes, lanes, policy outcomes, event types.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Use StrEnum or Literal for closed vocabularies; do not use free-form strings for known states.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.example:
class RiskLane(StrEnum):
    GREEN = auto()
    YELLOW = auto()
    RED = auto()

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: match on tagged unions plus assert_never
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Makes multi-variant logic visible and reviewable; helps type checkers catch missing cases.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.use_when: Closed domain states, command packet variants, route/event variants.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.avoid_when: Simple if/else is clearer or Python min version <3.10.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Use match only for structured variants; include an exhaustive fallback with assert_never when type checkers support it.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.example:
match event.kind:
    case EventKind.CREATED: ...
    case EventKind.DELETED: ...
    case other: assert_never(other)

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: contextlib.ExitStack for dynamic cleanup
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Prevents try/finally nests and leaked resources when number of resources is dynamic.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.use_when: Opening N files, layered tempdirs, dynamic mocks, multi-resource transactions.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.avoid_when: One obvious resource; use plain with.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: When acquiring variable numbers of resources, use ExitStack rather than manual cleanup lists.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.example:
with ExitStack() as stack:
    files = [stack.enter_context(path.open()) for path in paths]

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: pathlib.Path instead of string paths
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Gives agents a uniform path object and reduces cross-platform path bugs.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.avoid_when: Library explicitly requires a string, then convert at boundary.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Accept and return Path for filesystem code; convert strings at CLI/API edge.

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: contextvars for async/request-local context
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Avoids global mutable state bugs in async/server-style code.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.use_when: Request/session IDs, audit context, correlation IDs in async code.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Do not use globals for request/session context; use explicit parameters first, contextvars when propagation is needed.

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: raise ... from exc and exception notes
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Preserves causal chain and human-readable debugging context.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.use_when: Wrapping low-level errors into domain errors.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.avoid_when: You are deliberately hiding sensitive low-level details.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Wrap external errors with raise DomainError(...) from exc and add safe notes where useful.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.example:
except OSError as exc:
    raise ConfigLoadError(path) from exc

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: importlib.resources for packaged data
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Avoids fragile __file__ path hacks when reading package templates/resources.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Use importlib.resources.files(package) for package-owned assets instead of relative __file__ path traversal.

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: functools.singledispatch for conversion/plugin dispatch
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Replaces brittle if isinstance chains in adapter/conversion layers.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.use_when: Serialization/conversion from several known input classes.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.avoid_when: Domain logic should be explicit or variants are data tags not types.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Use singledispatch for type-based adapters, not for core business rules.

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: itertools pipelines for clear iteration
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Reduces hand-written index loops and off-by-one errors.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.use_when: Chunking, grouping, adjacent comparisons, streaming transforms.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Prefer itertools for standard iterator shapes; keep pipelines named and testable.

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: secrets for tokens and security randomness
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Prevents AI from using random for passwords, tokens, nonces, or session IDs.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Use secrets for security tokens; use random only for non-security simulation and tests.

underused_high_leverage_patterns.name: tomllib + dataclass Config
underused_high_leverage_patterns.why_advantage: Gives a standard config parser and typed internal config object.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.avoid_when: Need to write TOML; tomllib is read-only.
underused_high_leverage_patterns.prompt_rule: Parse TOML at the edge, validate, then convert to a typed config object.
